text: Mythcarver is a legendary longsword with a silvered blade that resonates with musical tones. It is one of the mystical artifacts known as the Vestiges of Divergence.

The Nein Heroez was the ship that the Mighty Nein salvaged and took command of after the destruction of the Balleater by a dragon turtle. It was called the Eden's Horizon until, on Veth's recommendation, the letters were rearranged into its new name.
The Midnight Hammer is an icebreaker hired by Vess DeRogna for her expedition with the Mighty Nein from Palebank Village to Balenpost.

Norad Firth was the captain of the ship The Brazen Beast. At some point in his life, he reminisced to an unidentified individual over the fact that, despite all of what he had seen throughout his life, he was still attracted to the "younger landscapes" of Tal'Dorei, but warned them to be wary and advised them to stick to the roads.

Mariner's Armor is a type of magical armor that has enchantments allowing its wearer to move underwater more effectively and buoying them to the surface if they fall unconscious. It is found as various types of armor. The Mighty Nein found a Mariner's Studded Leather in the sewers beneath Zadash. Its enchantment was transferred to Fjord's personal leather breastplate, now called a Mariner's Breastplate.
→ This page is about the ship. For the player character who is the ship's namesake, see Mollymauk Tealeaf. The Mollymauk is a ship captained by Kingsley Tealeaf.
The is a space ship and the setting for the one shot. It was used to ferry the Ark with the last of humanity in cryostasis to a fresh start on a new planet.
A is a bladed weapon that, when unsheathed in darkness, glows with moonlight.
Obsidian Flint Dragon Plate is a suit of magical armor worn by Arkhan.
An Oceanic Weapon is any ranged or thrown weapon used by the Water Ashari of Vesrah. It hasn't been featured on Critical Role yet.
The Plate of the Dawnmartyr is a set of armor and is one of the powerful Vestiges of Divergence.
was a halfling rogue/fighter member of the Iron Shepherds. As an NPC, was played by Matthew Mercer.

Pyremaul is a magical weapon and one of the Vestiges of Divergence. Forged from deep red iron, this massive hammer houses an everburning opal of eternal flame. It is rumored to be currently wielded by Grand Legate Phaestor, the fire giant ruler of Vulkanon, somewhere beneath the Cliffkeep Mountains. It has not yet appeared on Critical Role.

is the seventy-second episode of the third campaign of Critical Role. Bells Hells engage with a cursed pirate ship filled with ghosts, seeking passage across the waters of the Shattered Teeth, but a parley is not easily granted...
__NOTOC__ ]] of the Golden Hammer is the reiloran leader of the Volition. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.
Shale is a goliath fighter from the Herd of Storms. She was played by special guest Chris Perkins.

At some point, Grog almost got Trinket killed when he hit the bear's backside with the flat of his axe, startling him and sending him charging through a hallway full of traps, triggering every one of them in the process. Apart from that moment, Grog and Trinket are definitely buddies, as they wrestle playfully with each other, or eat papaya on the Slayer's Take Guild Hall floor. They also "tell jokes" to each other. Trinket was noticeably excited when Grog was revived from his coma in the Underdark. He ran up to nuzzle Grog, who hugged him around the neck and gave him a noogie.
Retort was a firearm created by Anna Ripley based on her eyewitness accounts of Percival de Rolo's gun, The List..
The Salty Criss was a pirate ship captained by Serack Feng. The ship was capsized by Caduceus using a Control Water spell while it was pursuing the Balleater.

A sailor, also known as a seafarer, is an individual who worked aboard a seagoing ship or vessel. The term was also used to describe crew members for skyships. The act of work aboard ships is called sailing.
is one of the crew of the Midnight Hammer, an icebreaker ship.
A is a shield with an eye engraved upon it, which grants the bearer particular awareness of their surroundings.

Ruin's Wake is a spear and one of the Arms of the Betrayers created by Gruumsh from the soul of a balor named Yarrowish. As a sentient weapon, it has a Chaotic Evil alignment and can communicate with its wielder telepathically. Similar to a Vestige of Divergence, Ruin's Wake progresses through various stages as it is wielded and gains new properties, including giving its wielder the ability to grant themselves and allies advantage on attack rolls, regain health by slaying their enemies, and summon lightning.

Seedling, the Wayward Pilgrim, is a well-made short sword originally given to Orym by his late husband Will. It was enchanted by Serataani, the Wildmother, in the temple of Zha'Vrollo following Chetney's trial there, gaining its magical abilities. It was later further enhanced by the Wildmother, becoming an exalted Relic of the Red Solstice.

A Scimitar of Speed is a magical sword with which one can make especially quick attacks. The wielder adds a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with the weapon, and can make an attack with it as a bonus action. Vox Machina and Lionel Gayheart defeated some Remnants in the Smouldercrown Mountains and found, in an unlocked chest, one such scimitar along with some other magic items that were being taken to Thar Amphala ahead of the ritual to bring back Vecna. This version of the sword was in Marquesian style, with pearlescent gems arrayed across the hilt. After Taryon Darrington identified the sword, it was passed around to see who could make good use of it, but no one was subsequently seen wielding it.
A ruidium weapon is any weapon infused with ruidium, which thereby conveys a variety of magic benefits but also the risk of ruidium corruption.

The Robe of the Midnight Rune is an enchanted robe that increases the wearer's base armor class, confers advantage against being charmed or frightened, and for a limited time increases their magical attack skills.
Scream Needle is a wicked curved dagger once wielded as an offhand weapon by Otohan Thull.
A ruidium shield, so called because it is infused with ruidium, thereby conveys a variety of magic benefits but also the risk of ruidium corruption.
Ruidium armor is a set of metallic armor infused with ruidium, which thereby conveys a variety of magic benefits but also the risk of ruidium corruption.

The Singing Dawnblade is a sword that Scanlan Shorthalt used before acquiring the legendary Mythcarver. Scanlan asked Kerrek to modify the scabbard to create a tiny storage slot, into which he inserted a dab of Scanlan's Poo of Scrying before giving the sword to his daughter, Kaylie.

The is a sentient, versatile black longsword once wielded by Kas the Bloody-Handed when he rebelled against Vecna. After Kas's death, the sword went missing in the depths of Thar Amphala until it was found and used by Vox Machina to help stop the reborn and ascended Vecna. The Sword of Kas seeks blood and the downfall of Vecna. As an NPC, the Sword is portrayed by Matthew Mercer.
is a smithy in Zadash owned and operated by Yannick Dumel and Jan. The smithy forged intricate items and had rows and racks of various pieces of armor and weapons on display on the inside.
The Sword of Fathoms was the name of the falchion Fjord was gifted by his patron Uk'otoa.
Star Razor, also known as Dwueth'var, is a sword from the Age of Arcanum and a Vestige of Divergence. Broken eons ago, the sword was reforged and is now in the possession of Fjord.
A shipping vessel or cargo ship was a type of ship that carried cargo from one port to another.

The Shield of Retribution is a silver and marble shield that was found by the Mighty Nein on the Yuan-ti abomination guarding the heart of the Temple of the False Serpent on Urukayxl. The item was custom made by Matthew Mercer.
Sweet Baby is a pistol owned by Veth Brenatto. She stole the gun from a guard in Hupperdook and later dismantled and reassembled it to learn how it works.
A Shield of Expression is shaped, on its front, in the semblance of a face. The expression of that face can be altered as a bonus action. It otherwise has the properties of a normal shield.
A staff of the adder is a staff that can be magically animated. Typically, a staff has one snake head, but Fearne Calloway's staff has two.
The Stahlmaster is a large clockwork mecha-suit created by Huron Stahlmast.
The Staff of Dark Odyssey is a magical staff that grants the wielder a bonus to magic and allows the casting of certain spells.

A Staff of Healing is a magical item that allows an attuned bard, cleric, or druid to expend charges to cast any of three spells: Cure Wounds (1 charge/spell level up to 4th), Lesser Restoration (2 charges), or Mass Cure Wounds (5 charges). The staff can hold 10 charges and regains 1d6 + 4 daily.
Sword wraiths are undead warriors haunting battlefields where they died without the honor they craved.
The Spire of Conflux, an ancient staff made by Melora's breath, allows the wielder to cast powerful spells. It is one of the legendary artifacts known as Vestiges of Divergence.
The Staff of Power is a magical staff wielded by Allura Vysoren during the Campaign of Vox Machina. Later, Allura loaned the staff to the Mighty Nein.
The List was Percival de Rolo's original pepperbox pistol, and the first gun he ever created under the influence of Orthax.

Teera is a halfling and a former bandit from the Ozmit Sea. She participated in a wyvern attack on the airship that Vox Machina used to travel to Vasselheim. After the fight, Teera was given the choice between death or joining the airship's crew at the lowest rank, and so started serving under Captain Damon. She eventually became a cherished part of the crew as the navigator due to her knowledge of the Ozmit Sea. As an NPC, she is played by Matthew Mercer.

Moradin, the All-Hammer, is the lawful good deity of craft, creation, family, and legacy. The All-Hammer is patron of craftsmen, blacksmiths, forgemasters, artisans, and miners, granting inspiration where respect and prayer are given. He shaped the mountains during the Founding, and stands as the patron of home and family.

The Shrew was a ship that sank in a storm near Glintshore around the year 510 PD. The ship carried Whisper, one of the Vestiges of Divergence. After learning about the Vestige's location by spying on Vox Machina through an enchantment on the pistol that had been taken from her, Anna Ripley hired a crew to search for the wreck of this ship to retrieve Whisper before they could. Ripley's crew succeeded a short time later.

The Mistake, formerly known as The Mist, is the ship formerly commanded by Captain Javeed Jawgrasp. Upon killing the captain and stealing the ship in Nicodranas, Fjord assumed the role of its captain under the moniker "Captain Tusktooth".
Ulfgar Fireforge is a dwarven fighter and member of Vox Moronica. He is played by Ify Nwadiwe.

Thorbir Falbek is a dwarven fighter and, as part of Vox Machina's initiation to the Slayer's Take guild, a temporary partner of Vax'ildan, Tiberius Stormwind, Keyleth, and Kashaw Vesh. Thorbir is played by special guest Wil Wheaton.
Travis Willingham is a human fighter from and . He is based on and played by the real Travis Willingham.
The Tinkertop Bolt Blaster 1000 is a prototype crossbow invented by Cleff Tinkertop of the city of Hupperdook. It was given to Nott as a reward for the Mighty Nein's aid in defeating the Gear Warden.
The Stormcap is a merchant ship captained by Jules Arog. The Mighty Nein, under the orders of Avantika, boarded the ship and stole its valuables.
is a dwarven blacksmith and forger of weapons and armor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
A trading ship, merchant ship, trade ship, or trade vessel was a type of ship that transported cargo, typically for a government or organization. One type of merchant ship was known as a coaster.
Turmoil is a magical weapon owned in 843 PD by Lord Ariks Eshteross and bequeathed by him to Bells Hells. Thereafter it was wielded by Chetney Pock O'Pea.
is a human blacksmith in Zephrah, and a craftsman of fine weapons and armor. As an NPC, is played by Matthew Mercer.
Truthbearer is magical plate armor that once belonged to the fabled Uther Vendrock.

Thresher is a two-part miniseries set on board the deep-sea submarine S.S. Thresher on a mission to explore the long-abandoned Rán-Beor Station, "a geothermal energy facility resting in the ocean’s unforgiving depths—silent, decayed, and waiting. As pressure mounts both literally and figuratively, the crew must battle the claustrophobia of a metal tube, the terror of lurking behemoths, and the increasing paranoia of mutinous cabin-mates."

The Whitestone Rifle Corps are an elite Whitestone military unit founded by Lord Percival de Rolo. Unlike the Paleguard, the guardsmen of Whitestone who answer to the Chamber of Whitestone, the Whitestone Rifle Corps are royal guardsmen that are assigned specifically to protect Whitestone Castle and the de Rolo family. Members are trained in the use of a musket or a pistol as their primary weapon with the restriction of only wielding them while patrolling the city walls or castle battlements, excluding emergency scenarios or precedents permitted by the Chamber of Whitestone. Though Percy was initially opposed to the notion of mass producing his firearms inventions, after his battle with (and death by) Dr. Anna Ripley, he realized that it was inevitable that others would develop his guns and use them to their advantage. Realizing Whitestone needed to take advantage of such technology before it became widespread, Percy distributed Ripley's rifles to (as well as constructed new firearms for) these new Riflemen. Originally, the corps was a company of roughly a dozen musketeers, including both men and women. By 843 PD the Corps had grown to at least 50 riflemen. Their uniform consists of dark-stained leathers with shoulder cloaks and leather hats with one side pinned up. The Rifle Corps has a special undercover unit reporting directly to the de Rolo family, called the Whitestone Hunters. These soldiers loyally serve as spies, bodyguards, and even assassins if necessary.
The Waste Hunter Blade was a "gnarly-looking" magical curved hooked longsword wielded by the drow infiltrator Thuron.
A is a magic weapon that deals additional damage on a natural 20 attack roll.
A vorpal sword is a greatsword, longsword or scimitar that can behead opponents on lucky strikes.
A Weapon of Warning is a magical weapon of any kind that has been enchanted to provide its wielder with warning of nearby dangers.

The War of Axe and Vine is an aggregate term for multiple conflicts over the political boundaries of the continent taking place in many places in Pasitar that began in the 37th year of the Age of Mortals and ended approximately 26 years before the events of Campaign Four, in the year 45. It resulted in establishing the boundaries of the new nations of Timmony, Baladri, Theyk, Ledlow, Atleron, Macara, Equilaine, and Rhusk.
A walker's ward is a small charm created by the druids of Aramán, used to conceal the wearer's thoughts and their true nature from several kinds of magical detection.
The Zephyr Armor is a light protective garment that bolsters the movements of its wearer with gentle currents of wind.

Daniel; Peter Nguyen | First = Deathstroke Vol 3 7 | Overview = The God Killer is a sword created by Hephaestus that can, as the name implies, kill Gods. | HistoryText = To follow through on a Fallen God's final request should he ever meet his demise, the Greek forge deity Hephaestus offered the lethal assassin Deathstroke a contract in the assassination of an old foe of Olympus named Lapetus, a Greek Titan. As Slade was mortal, he was granted the use of this sword to enable him to fight and kill gods. The sword holds many wondrous attributes, although its primary directive is the slaying of immortals. To some degree it also possesses a consciousness of its own, capable of altering its physical form. Grail possessed the blade during her usurpation of the throne of Themyscira from Hippolyta, and upon her defeat, it was stolen by Lex Luthor who later gave it to the Cheetah as part of his plans. Pennyworth is an action crime thriller television series developed by Bruno Heller and Danny Cannon, and produced by DC Entertainment. It stars Jack Bannon as the title character, a former British SAS soldier working with American intelligence to take down a rising fascist party in 1960s London. The series aired on from 2019 to 2021, with its third and final season streaming on HBO Max in 2022. It serves as a prequel to Gotham (2014–2019) and also draws elements from the graphic novel V for Vendetta (1989).

Powerless was an American television series focusing on the staff of Wayne Security, a subsidiary of Wayne Enterprises that uses R&D to protect civilians from superpowered damage. It was canceled after airing nine of the twelve completed episodes. The remaining episodes were released on [https://www.tvnz.co.nz/ TVNZ on Demand].

{{DC Database:Publisher Template | Image = Wildstorm logo.JPG | Status = Active | Founded = 1992 | Founders = Jim Lee | Current Staff = Jim Lee | Former Staff = | Location = Los Angeles | Industry = Comics | Overview = WildStorm Productions, or simply "Wildstorm," was a publishing studio. In 1999, Jim Lee and WildStorm left Image, and Lee sold WildStorm to DC Comics. After the sale, Lee remained as Wildstorm's Editorial Director. The Executive Editor was Scott Dunbier. Blade Barrage has two to three different uses. The first way is used by Hunters and by extent players where the Hunter leaps into the air and throws two sets of five knives which explode shortly after embedding themselves on the first person or surface they touch. Cayde-6 used a variation of this Blade Barrage when he fought the Scorn where he threw both pairs at once. The other version is used by Lightbearer Acolytes where instead of being an instant-use Super, it is a transformation Super where the Acolyte dodges from side to side, summoning five Karambits along the dodge path. Once the dodge is finished the Acolyte strikes a pose, causing the Karambits to fire towards the target and explode on impact instead of embedding themselves first. The acolyte can preform this attack up to three times before the super ends.

Dustwalker Cloak is a legendary cloak manufactured by the Vanguard, and is part of the Dustwalker armor set. It can be purchased from Cayde-6.
Dustwalker is a pair of legendary Hunter gauntlets manufactured by the Vanguard, and is part of the Dustwalker armor set. It can be purchased from Cayde-6.
Efrideet's Spear is a legendary sniper rifle. It can be obtained from the Iron Banner event.
Dredgen Yor, formerly known as Rezyl Azzir, was a Titan and the creator of the exotic hand cannon Thorn, which he created using his old hand cannon Rose.

Hotfix 1.0.2.2, which went live Tuesday October 14 at approximately 17:00 GMT, introduces a number of weapon balance changes across archetypes, specific weapons, plus fixes to the Templar encounter in Vault of Glass.
Echo 33 is a rare pulse rifle obtained as a random completion reward.

Update 1.1 went live on Monday, December 1, 2014 shortly after 18:00 GMT. This update included Exotic weapon buffs, additional acquisition paths for destination upgrade materials, changes to exotic gear upgrades in preparation for The Dark Below, and corrections to issues introduced by the recent update to Vault of Glass.
Deathsinger's Mantle is a piece of legendary Warlock chest armor that can be obtained from the Bridge on Crota's End raid.
Do Gooder V is a legendary auto rifle added in The Dark Below. It can be purchased from Arcite 99-40.

Eidolon Ally is a legendary auto rifle added in The Dark Below. It is obtained by activating the "Cannibalism" talent on the Husk of the Pit. The Eidolon Ally can be upgraded to the exotic auto rifle Necrochasm using a Crux of Crota. It also requires 12 Ascendant Energy & 32 Relic Icon before proceeding with the Crux.
Doom Echo XI is a rare sniper rifle that can be received as a random completion award or through an engram.
Deathsinger's Gaze is a legendary Warlock helmet that can be obtained from killing Crota in the Crota's End raid.
Dusk Tread is a legendary armor set built for the Warlock class by the Vanguard. The set can be purchased from Ikora Rey.
Deathsinger's Herald is a set of legendary Warlock leg armor. It can be obtained as a random loot drop from the Bridge in the Crota's End raid.
Update 1.1.1 rebalanced the weapon sandbox and fixed issues with several perks. It was released on February 25, 2015.

Dusk Tread III is legendary chest armor able to be wielded by Warlocks. Dusk Tread III can be dismantled to generate Glimmer, Armor Materials, and Legendary Marks. It can also be transferred to other characters through the vault.

Dusk Tread VI is legendary Warlock leg armor. Dusk Tread VI can be dismantled to generate Glimmer, Armor Materials, and Legendary Marks. It can also be transferred to other characters through the vault.

Dusk Tread VII is a legendary helmet able to be wielded by Warlocks. Dusk Tread VII can be dismantled to generate Glimmer, Armor Materials, and Legendary Marks. It can also be transferred to other characters through the vault.
Double Nickel is a rare shotgun. It can be dismantled to generate Glimmer and Weapon Parts.
Dreg's Promise is an exotic sidearm introduced in the House of Wolves expansion. It could be obtained from the exotic weapon bounty The Elder Cipher. The weapon fires in 3-round bursts.
Dispatch I11 is a legendary auto rifle introduced in the House of Wolves expansion. It can be obtained as a reward in the Vanguard Dragon Playlist.

Empyrean Bellicose is an exotic helmet which can be equipped by Titans. It can be dismantled to generate Glimmer, Armor Materials and an Exotic Shard. It can also be transferred between characters using the Vault.

Dead Light Plate is a legendary chest armor which can be equipped by Titans. It can be dismantled to generate Glimmer, Armor Materials, and Legendary Marks. It can also be transferred between characters using the Vault.

Dead Light Vest is a legendary chest armor which can be equipped by Hunters. It can be dismantled to generate Glimmer, Armor Materials, and Legendary Marks. It can also be transferred between characters using the Vault.
